title: Led a cross-team data initiative
body: Tell me about a time you led a cross-functional data project. What was the goal, who was involved, and what was the outcome?
framework:
**Situation:** A pipeline serving finance and product had conflicting SLAs and no single owner.

**Task:** Align stakeholders and deliver a unified bronze-to-gold model without breaking existing reports.

**Action:** Ran a kickoff with schema contracts, set weekly demos, split work into ingestion (your team) vs consumption (BI), documented decisions in Confluence.

**Result:** Cut duplicate pipelines by 40%, finance sign-off in 6 weeks, adopted as template for other domains.

**Tip:** Quantify scope (tables, users, latency) and name tools (ADF, Databricks, dbt).

title: Worked with a difficult stakeholder
body: Describe a situation where you had to work closely with a stakeholder who was skeptical of your approach. How did you handle it?
framework:
**Situation:** Product manager wanted real-time dashboards; your batch lakehouse couldn't meet sub-minute latency.

**Task:** Find a workable compromise without over-engineering.

**Action:** Mapped their actual decision windows (hourly, not second-level), proposed incremental loads + materialized views, showed prototype with sample data.

**Result:** PM accepted hourly refresh; you avoided costly streaming build. Relationship improved through transparent trade-off doc.

**Tip:** Show empathy first, then data-driven alternatives — never blame the stakeholder.

title: Disagreement on architecture
body: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague or architect on a technical decision. How did you resolve it?
framework:
**Situation:** Team debated Spark vs SQL stored procedures for a 50M-row daily transform.

**Task:** Pick an approach that balances maintainability, cost, and team skills.

**Action:** Built a one-day POC for both paths, compared cost (DBU vs SQL DWU), runtime, and testability. Presented findings neutrally in architecture review.

**Result:** Chose Databricks for complex joins; kept SQL for simple aggregations. Documented decision ADR; both sides felt heard.

**Tip:** Focus on criteria, not personalities. "We" language throughout.

title: Pipeline failure in production
body: Tell me about a time a data pipeline failed in production. What happened and what did you learn?
framework:
**Situation:** Nightly ADF pipeline failed silently — downstream dashboard showed stale data for 2 days.

**Task:** Restore freshness and prevent recurrence.

**Action:** Traced to schema drift (new nullable column broke strict mapping), added schema evolution + alerting on row-count deltas, wrote runbook for on-call.

**Result:** MTTR dropped from 48h to 2h; zero repeat incidents in 6 months.

**Tip:** Own the failure without drama. Emphasize monitoring, blameless postmortem, and systemic fix.

title: Tight deadline migration
body: Describe a project with a very tight deadline. How did you prioritize and deliver?
framework:
**Situation:** 3-week mandate to migrate on-prem SQL Server ETL to Azure before license renewal.

**Task:** Move critical 12 pipelines without data loss.

**Action:** MoSCoW prioritization, parallelized lift-and-shift for simple jobs, deferred nice-to-have transforms, daily standups with business sponsor.

**Result:** 10/12 pipelines live on day 20; remaining 2 in hypercare week 4. Zero missed SLAs.

**Tip:** Show ruthless scope control and communication cadence.

title: Data quality crisis
body: Tell me about a time you discovered a serious data quality issue. How did you investigate and fix it?
framework:
**Situation:** Revenue metrics dropped 15% overnight — executives assumed product issue.

**Task:** Determine if data or business caused the drop.

**Action:** Compared source vs warehouse row counts, found duplicate dedup logic removed valid multi-currency rows; quarantined bad partition, replayed from bronze, added reconciliation checks.

**Result:** Metrics restored in 4 hours; exec briefing prevented wrong product decisions. DQ framework expanded to all fact tables.

**Tip:** DE stories shine when you saved business from bad decisions.

title: Proposed a process improvement
body: Give an example of when you identified and implemented a process improvement without being asked.
framework:
**Situation:** Engineers manually deployed notebooks; drift between dev and prod caused weekly incidents.

**Task:** Introduce CI/CD for data assets with minimal disruption.

**Action:** Piloted Git-backed Databricks Repos + Azure DevOps pipeline for 2 notebooks, documented template, trained team in lunch-and-learn.

**Result:** Deployment time 2h → 15min; prod incidents down 60% in Q2.

**Tip:** Show you drive change bottom-up with proof, not mandates.

title: Explained technical concept to non-technical audience
body: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex data concept to non-technical stakeholders.
framework:
**Situation:** Legal team needed to understand PII masking in the lakehouse for GDPR audit.

**Task:** Explain encryption, tokenization, and access controls without jargon.

**Action:** Used analogy (locked filing cabinet + key per role), diagrammed bronze/silver/gold with redacted samples, walked through audit log demo.

**Result:** Legal signed off; you became go-to for compliance questions.

**Tip:** Analogies + visuals beat acronyms. Confirm understanding with questions.

title: Mentored a junior engineer
body: Describe a time you mentored someone less experienced. What was your approach and the outcome?
framework:
**Situation:** New grad struggled with PySpark window functions on a customer churn model.

**Task:** Upskill them while meeting sprint deadline.

**Action:** Pair-programmed 2 sessions, left commented notebook templates, assigned smaller partition of problem, reviewed PRs with constructive feedback.

**Result:** They owned next window-function story solo; promoted to mid-level within a year.

**Tip:** Balance support with autonomy — show growth metrics.

title: Collaborated under pressure
body: Tell me about a time your team had to collaborate intensely to meet a critical business need.
framework:
**Situation:** Black Friday — marketing needed hourly campaign performance; existing pipeline was daily.

**Task:** Enable near-real-time feeds in 5 days with analytics and infra teams.

**Action:** Split streams (ingestion vs dashboard), shared Slack war room, hourly checkpoints, feature-flagged new path parallel to old.

**Result:** Hourly dashboard live day before launch; 0 downtime during peak; reused pattern for Cyber Monday.

**Tip:** Highlight coordination mechanics and risk mitigation (parallel run).

title: Pushed back on unrealistic requirements
body: Describe a time you had to push back on requirements that were unrealistic or poorly defined.
framework:
**Situation:** Business asked for "real-time 360° customer view" in 2 weeks with 200 source systems.

**Task:** Reset expectations without killing the initiative.

**Action:** Documented effort estimate, proposed MVP (top 5 sources, 15-min latency), showed phased roadmap with cost per phase.

**Result:** Sponsors approved 8-week MVP; full vision became FY roadmap item.

**Tip:** Replace "no" with "yes, if we phase it" — always offer a path.

title: Missed a personal deadline
body: Tell me about a time you missed a deadline or deliverable. What did you do?
framework:
**Situation:** Underestimated complexity of CDC from Oracle; sprint commitment slipped by 4 days.

**Task:** Minimize impact and rebuild trust.

**Action:** Flagged risk at day 2 (not day 4), negotiated scope cut (deferred history backfill), worked with DBA for faster log access, daily updates to PM.

**Result:** Incremental load delivered on revised date; retrospective improved estimation templates.

**Tip:** Early escalation beats surprise. Show learning, not excuses.

title: Designed a new data model
body: Walk me through a time you designed or redesigned a data model. What trade-offs did you consider?
framework:
**Situation:** Star schema couldn't support evolving product attributes (SCD Type 2 explosion).

**Task:** Redesign customer dimension for flexibility and query performance.

**Action:** Evaluated wide table vs normalized bridge; chose hybrid with current-state view + history table; documented grain and PK strategy.

**Result:** Query time -30%, analyst self-serve improved; pattern reused across 3 domains.

**Tip:** Name dimensional modeling concepts — interviewers listen for grain, SCD, denormalization rationale.

title: Managed scope creep
body: Tell me about a project where scope kept expanding. How did you manage it?
framework:
**Situation:** "Simple" Salesforce ingest became 15 custom objects mid-sprint.

**Task:** Protect timeline and team morale.

**Action:** Introduced change-request log, weekly scope review with sponsor, traded low-priority objects for phase 2, froze scope 5 days before release.

**Result:** Phase 1 on time with 10 objects; phase 2 planned and funded.

**Tip:** Formalize change control — shows maturity beyond coding.

title: Presented to leadership
body: Describe a time you presented technical work or recommendations to senior leadership.
framework:
**Situation:** CTO asked why cloud data costs spiked 40% QoQ.

**Task:** Explain root cause and remediation in 10 minutes.

**Action:** One-slide executive summary (cost drivers pie chart), 3 recommendations with ROI, avoided cluster config deep-dive unless asked.

**Result:** Approved auto-termination policy and reserved capacity; costs flat next quarter.

**Tip:** Lead with business impact, bury technical detail in appendix.

title: Onboarded to a new team
body: Tell me about joining a new team or project. How did you ramp up and contribute quickly?
framework:
**Situation:** Joined Azure data platform team mid-migration; unfamiliar with their ADF naming conventions.

**Task:** Become productive within 2 weeks.

**Action:** Shadowed on-call, mapped pipeline dependency diagram, fixed 3 small bugs in week 1, proposed doc for naming standards.

**Result:** Owned first feature in week 3; doc adopted team-wide.

**Tip:** Show proactive learning and quick wins — not passive onboarding.

title: Optimized a slow pipeline
body: Tell me about a time you significantly improved pipeline performance or cost.
framework:
**Situation:** Daily Spark job on 2TB logs took 4 hours and blocked downstream SLA.

**Task:** Cut runtime below 90 minutes without correctness loss.

**Action:** Profiled stages, fixed skew with salting, switched to Delta OPTIMIZE + Z-order, right-sized cluster, partitioned by date.

**Result:** Runtime 75 min, cost -35%, SLA met consistently.

**Tip:** Before/after numbers are mandatory. Mention specific Spark/Delta knobs.

title: Drove adoption of a new tool
body: Describe a time you introduced a new technology or tool to your team. How did you drive adoption?
framework:
**Situation:** Team used ad-hoc SQL scripts; no version control or testing.

**Task:** Introduce dbt for transform layer with buy-in from skeptics.

**Action:** Migrated one low-risk mart as showcase, ran internal demo showing tests + lineage, paired with strongest skeptic on second model.

**Result:** 80% of transforms on dbt within 3 months; incident rate from bad deploys dropped.

**Tip:** Champions + proof project beat top-down mandates.

title: Received critical feedback
body: Tell me about a time you received difficult feedback. How did you respond?
framework:
**Situation:** Manager said your documentation was blocking handoffs during PTO.

**Task:** Improve without defensiveness.

**Action:** Asked for specific examples, created runbook template, scheduled doc review in Definition of Done, peer-reviewed next 3 pipelines.

**Result:** Handoff survey scores improved; became team doc standard bearer.

**Tip:** Growth mindset stories — thank the feedback, show behavior change.

title: Built something beyond your job description
body: Give an example of going above and beyond your formal responsibilities.
framework:
**Situation:** Analysts filed weekly tickets for the same metric definitions.

**Task:** Not in your role, but you saw repeated pain.

**Action:** Built internal metrics catalog in Confluence with SQL snippets, linked to dbt docs, ran 30-min office hours.

**Result:** Duplicate tickets -70%; promoted to "data champion" for analytics org.

**Tip:** Connect extra effort to org-wide impact — shows senior potential.
